In the wake of the historic midterm elections that saw a collapse of the
Republican Party and a resurgence of the Democrats, observers may have
expected the 2028 presidential campaign to already be underway.

For now, though, potential Democratic candidates and their allies are
anxiously twiddling their thumbs, holding off on deciding their political
plans until Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez decides whether to run.

"We're just all on pause until AOC decides something," one Democratic analyst
tells **Zeteo**.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Thousands of people in all 50 states have already mobilized to help push the
young democratic socialist to run for president. While some on the left are
wary of an AOC run - whether it be out of concerns about electability, or
their own strategic disagreements with Ocasio-Cortez - she's their biggest
star, and seemingly their best bet.

The midterm results - some of which Ocasio-Cortez helped fashion with her
relentless campaigning - suggest an AOC run is no longer a moonshot. And that
reality is one even Republicans have come to fear.
